title: Install Paperboy and select production schedules
summary: Install Paperboy, initialize its TOML production definitions, apply Clockwork activation snapshots, and explicitly enable or disable production schedules.
use_when: Install or update Paperboy, initialize or validate its production definitions, publish configured schedules, inspect schedule selection, or control one selected production.
do_not_use_when: The request is to execute a production now, retry a saved email, modify another product, or infer inbox delivery.
outcome: Matching Paperboy programs and provider bytes are selected; configured productions have exact Clockwork schedule selections with preserved existing enabled intent and new production schedules disabled.

interfaces.label: Enable future scheduling for one production
Disable future scheduling for one production

effects: Installation selects matching program and provider files, initializes only a missing default production-definition file, and applies configured schedule snapshots. It does not execute renderers or send their output.

Apply registers all definitions before binding changes, preserves existing enabled intent, leaves new production schedules disabled, and disables removed schedules without deleting history or incidents. Explicit enable permits future renderer executions and email.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Paperboy/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.
authority: Paperboy owns its production definitions and schedule selection. Clockwork owns atomic per-key transitions, runtime history, overlap and failure halts. Cell deployment owns instruction execution and retained receipts; renderer and Email success remain separate.
success: Initialization succeeds when the absent production-definition file is written or existing valid configuration is preserved. Apply succeeds after every requested selection and removal transition completes. Installation succeeds when declared instructions complete. None establishes renderer correctness, future timer delivery, or inbox receipt.
failure_and_recovery: Applying several production schedules is not atomic. Earlier successful transitions remain after a later failure. Inspect schedule status, correct the reported problem, and reapply the same production-definition file. Retain Clockwork history and established incidents.
Failed deployment retains completed effects and executes no automatic rollback or recovery. Inspect retained evidence before an explicitly authorized new attempt.
An established scheduling halt requires exact incident approval through Clockwork. Enable, disable, apply, and installation do not clear it. Approval does not retry a renderer or uncertain email.
privacy: Manifests, schedule arguments, paths, subjects, and logs are private local data. Clockwork retains activation metadata, not renderer bodies.
does_not_authorize: Catalog presence does not authorize installation, enabling a production schedule, deleting retained state, retrying email, or clearing a failure incident.

consumers.statement: The current user and authorized Cell product-deployment operations.

preconditions.statement: Submit ./ci.sh submit COMMIT --deploy paperboy from the Cell root. CI and Telete are the sole deployment route. Select required dependency updates explicitly. Schedule operations require installed Paperboy and supported Clockwork. Script execution and schedule enable require separate standing authority.

inputs.statement: An absolute --manifest path or the default production-definition file and literal configured production definitions. Enable and disable require one production ID; status accepts an optional ID. Init writes an empty version-one production-definition file only if absent. Installation accepts no product settings and always uses the default production-definition file. The selected production-definition file governs the complete paperboy/ binding namespace; alternate paths do not isolate bindings.

outputs.statement: Configured-production validation, immutable activation definition selections, binding enabled and halt metadata, aggregate local status evidence, and retained deployment instruction outcomes. These observations do not run a renderer. Default output uses production labels; --json retains compatible jobs fields. The raw Iatreion snapshot uses aggregate unit paperboy/productions, while individual Clockwork binding keys remain unchanged.

data_semantics.statement: The production-definition file is configuration authority; applied activation definitions are scheduled command snapshots. Existing production schedules retain enabled intent, new schedules are disabled, and removed schedules retain disabled selection and history. Status represents retained binding metadata rather than guaranteed future activation. Scheduled logs can retain result metadata, including an accepted provider message ID, but no body or structured send-recovery ledger.

identity_and_units.statement: Each stable production ID maps to paperboy/PRODUCTION_ID. Changing its production definition changes the immutable activation definition; renaming it creates a different binding. Durations use whole seconds and calendar schedules use the host local hour and minute.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Apply validates all configured productions and registers their definitions before binding mutations. Status reads selected Clockwork metadata at invocation. The product aggregate status-snapshot describes production definitions and readiness, not each dynamic binding or execution history. Initialization validates and preserves an existing production-definition file rather than replacing it.
No maximum activation delay, catch-up count, or final email-delivery latency is promised.

access.statement: Current-user local interfaces use the provider-owned Clockwork and Email clients. Scheduled definitions launch the exact installed Paperboy program from the product root; renderer launch context is defined by paperboy.report.send. launchd schedule delivery requires a macOS GUI login domain.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One schedule lock serializes Paperboy mutations. Clockwork provides per-key transition atomicity; applying several production schedules retains earlier completed transitions after failure. Identical selections need no transition. Disable retains definitions and incidents, and no apply enables a new production schedule.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Paperboy/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.

operational_limits.statement: Production-definition file maximum 1 MiB. Per-production schedules use overlap skip, run-at-load false, and a 1380-second outer timeout. Different productions can run concurrently. Interval range is 1 through 31536000 seconds; local hour 0 through 23 and minute 0 through 59. Logs append under the private Paperboy logs directory.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Installation selects production schedules. The version-one TOML production-definition file is the configuration authority. Product installation and Clockwork selection remain separate from renderer execution. The preferred productions table and legacy jobs table select the same definitions; combining both in one file is rejected. Existing files are not rewritten. Retained --job runner snapshots remain valid alongside new --production snapshots. JSON result keys remain compatible.
No general future compatibility or deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: The Paperboy renderer feature defines production-definition input, execution, exact stdout handoff, email success, privacy, and limits.
Clockwork supplies definition registration, exact binding transitions, scheduling, overlap, runtime records, incidents, and continuation approval.
Email supplies the selected fixed-recipient wrapper and submission boundary; applying a schedule does not test credentials or send.

Telete validates, prepares signed programs and executes explicitly selected ordered product instructions. It retains source and request correlation and process outcomes. Products own setup, state, maintenance and recovery.
